title: The Miraculous Medal (1830)
hookLine: Catherine Labouré's vision in Paris: O Mary, conceived without sin

lines: A SMALL OVAL ON A CHAIN.
TWO HEARTS AND A RING OF STARS.
WHERE DID THE DESIGN COME FROM?
cards: A small oval of stamped metal, on a thin chain, tucked under a nurse's scrubs. Pressed into the palm of someone in a hospital bed by a grandmother who says, just keep it.

On the back, a whole picture: a letter, a cross, two hearts, a ring of stars. On the front, a woman with light pouring from her hands, and a line of words around the edge. And the design wasn't dreamed up by a jeweler.
It came from a young woman's account of one night in Paris.

teach.h: A NOVICE IN PARIS, A VISION AT NIGHT.
teach.b: First, the vision. Catherine was a young novice with the Daughters of Charity in Paris.
By her own account, Mary appeared to her standing on a globe, with rays of light streaming from her hands, an oval of words around her.
Then it turned to show the back, and she was told to have a medal struck after that model.
Her confessor was cautious, but the medal was made, and the story goes that Catherine told almost no one it was her, and spent her years quietly caring for old men in a hospice.
Second, the words on the front: "O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee."
That's the Immaculate Conception, which you met back in year one: the Church teaches that Mary, from the first moment of her life, was kept free from original sin, by the grace of her son.
It's about Mary's beginning, not Jesus's birth. A later pope defined it as dogma, and the medal's admirers note that its words said it first. Third, the back.
A letter M with a cross rising out of it. Below, two hearts: one ringed with thorns, for Jesus, and one pierced by a sword, for Mary.

teach.h: AN M, A CROSS, TWO HEARTS, TWELVE STARS.
teach.b: Around them, twelve stars, which readers connect to the woman in the Apocalypse, in the Douay-Rheims: "on her head a crown of twelve stars." Fourth, the name.
People called it miraculous because of the cures and conversions they reported.

teach.h: NOT A CHARM: A REMINDER YOU WEAR.
teach.b: The Church is careful: a medal isn't a charm, and it does nothing by itself.

teach.h: PRAY FOR US WHO HAVE RECOURSE TO THEE.
teach.b: It's a reminder you can wear.

how: Catholics wear the Miraculous Medal on a chain or carry it, often blessed by a priest, and say its short prayer, "O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee."

o: a medal the pope awards for a proven healing
a medal designed from Catherine's vision in Paris
a medal said to cure anyone who wears it

games.q: the medal, front and back — tap the pairs.
p: the novice who saw the vision
one with thorns, one with a sword

s: conceived without sin is about the virgin birth of Jesus
it names the Immaculate Conception: Mary kept free from original sin from the first moment of her own life.
the back of the medal shows an M with a cross above it
an M, a cross rising out of it, two hearts below, twelve stars around.
the Church teaches the medal works by itself, like a charm
a medal does nothing by itself. it's a reminder you wear, and a prayer.

games.q: you're a young novice. you've seen a vision and been told to have a medal made. what do you do?
o: announce it to all of Paris.
tell your confessor, and let it go forward quietly.
games.why: Catherine went to her confessor, who was cautious. the medal was made, and the story goes she stayed hidden, caring for old men in a hospice.

practice: Hold a medal, or whatever you carry close, a ring, a cross, a key, and let it stand for someone you'd like to keep close today.
If you pray, say the medal's line slowly: O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee; if not, simply hold the object, and the person, and breathe.

wordCard.voice: The Miraculous Medal. The medal from Saint Catherine's account in Paris: Mary's prayer around the front, an M, a cross, two hearts and twelve stars on the back. Today's word.

orig.note: French: O Mary, conceived without sin, the start of the medal's inscription.

carryVoice: Your line: conceived without sin. Mary's beginning, kept whole by grace. Rest well.
